description_full: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc., a financial institution, provides a range of financial services for corporations, financial institutions, governments, and individuals in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. It operates through three segments: Global Banking & Markets, Asset & Wealth Management, and Platform Solutions. The Global Banking & Markets segment provides financial advisory services, including strategic advisory assignments related to mergers and acquisitions, divestitures, corporate defense activities, restructurings, and spin-offs; equity and debt underwriting of public offerings and private placements; relationship lending and acquisition financing; secured lending through structured credit and asset-backed lending, such as warehouse, residential and commercial mortgage, corporate, consumer, auto, and student loans; financing through securities purchased under agreements to resell; and commodity financing through structured transactions. This segment also offers client execution activities for cash and derivative instruments; credit and interest rate products; and provision of mortgages, currencies, commodities, and equities related products. Its Asset & Wealth Management segment manages assets across various classes, including equity, fixed income, hedge funds, credit funds, private equity, real estate, currencies, commodities, and asset allocation strategies; and provides customized investment advisory solutions, wealth advisory services, personalized financial planning, and private banking services, as well as invests in corporate equity, credit, real estate, and infrastructure assets. The Platform Solutions segment offers credit cards; and transaction banking and other services, such as deposit-taking, payment solutions, and other cash management services for corporate and institutional clients. The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. was founded in 1869 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

financial_summary: Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (The) is a mega-cap financial services business with a $249.7B market cap on $58.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 4% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
The company is burning through $47.2B of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.3× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 7.1% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

Fintech disintermediation — neobanks, embedded finance, and blockchain rails are unbundling the fee streams that traditional banks took for granted.
Interest rate regime shifts — a rapid move in rates can invert the yield curve, crush bond portfolios, and trigger deposit flight simultaneously.

sect: Its 37% operating margin runs 8pp above the Financial Services median (29%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.45x).
It accounts for 1.4% of sector revenue and 2.1% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.02 across 512 companies in the universe; the top four hold 20% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 16% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 15% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 25% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 33% and a beta of 1.19, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $1.8B traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 46% in the 2020 crash, 31% in the 2022 bear market and 75% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its blended-model fair value of $445 (margin of safety -94%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 29%), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 110% above its 10-year median.
The 21 covering analysts target $1,031 on average, 19% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 4% falls short of the cost of capital of 10.7%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.35).
As a lender it runs a net interest margin of 1.78% and an efficiency ratio of 38% (lean).
It earns a 14% return on equity.
hlth: CET1 capital of 13.5% sits comfortably above the ~7% regulatory minimum with buffer.
Non-performing loans are 1.04% of the book.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 7.2% over 3 years, 5.5% over 5 years and 5.6% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 14%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.6%), and institutions hold 76%.
Insider trading is two-way: 2 purchases and 36 sales over the past year, net $4.2M sold.
It returns 7.1% a year to shareholders (4.9% in buybacks and 2.3% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 2.9% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 26 consecutive years, raising it 17.7% a year over the last five.
people: With about 47,500 employees, each generates about $1.2M of revenue, 2.5x the Financial Services median, and productivity has risen 4.5% a year.
Free cash flow is negative, at -$994K per employee.
CEO pay is $13.6M (11x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (10/10, lower is better).
